A twenty-five-year-old walked into a New York bank and asked for twenty-two million dollars. She said she was a German heiress with a sixty million euro fortune. There was just one problem. The fortune did not exist. New York, 2013. A young woman lands in the city during fashion week. Her name, she said, was Anna Delvey. And New York believed her. She handed waiters and doormen hundred dollar bills. Because Anna had a dream. A private club for the art world, called the Anna Delvey Foundation. So she asked a Manhattan bank for a loan of twenty-two million dollars. As proof, she showed statements from Swiss accounts holding sixty million euros. She had made them herself. Then the bills started piling up. She chartered a private jet, and the thirty-five thousand dollar bill was never paid. Act rich, move fast, and be gone before anyone checks. But one trip would bring it all down. Follow for part two.
